| [ADR-126](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-126.md) | A reference may name several schemes | `scheme:` on a reference takes a list as well as a string, and a code passes if it belongs to any scheme listed. A string is a list of one, so no config changes meaning. A converse is a field of the same name on every scheme listed, each naming the declaring scheme back; a chain walks the relation only when its own scheme is the sole target. Rejected: a field per target family, a loose `requires` field, a refinement predicate language, and letting a chain walk a union that includes its scheme. | Proposed |
| [ADR-127](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-127.md) | A logic core in clingo, behind a procedural shell | The parts of luria that decide things about the record's graph — converse pairs, invariants, chain edges, config consistency, and which acknowledgement answers for a citation — move from hand-written Python walks to Answer Set Programming rules evaluated by clingo, over facts the Python extracts. Python keeps parsing, rendering, editing, git and the network, and turns derived facts into findings, edits and pages. The move is one subsystem at a time, each held to byte-identical `luria lint` and `luria index` output against the last release on every real record. Rejected: a full rewrite, Cypher or an embedded graph database, SQLite recursive CTEs, a hand-rolled Datalog evaluator, and staying in Python. | Proposed |
| [ADR-128](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-128.md) | Configuration is the only source of relation semantics | No relation is supplied by the code: the successor and influenced_by become ordinary declared references, roles point at declarations instead of creating them, references may target declared remotes, the facts give every reference value a declared type, and relations.lp no longer infers a type from an absence. luria upgrade explicit-relations writes down what older versions supplied. Rejected: emitting the built-ins as facts, an explicit any-scheme target, and undeclared roles with the old defaults. | Proposed |
| [ADR-129](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-129.md) v2 | A chain may walk a named path pattern | A record may declare named path patterns in Cypher's pattern syntax, such as `(b:CLAIM)<-[:concludes]-(i:INF)<-[:premise_of]-(a:CLAIM)`. Node labels are schemes, edge types are reference fields, and a hop holds when the relation does as `held/4` reads it. luria parses patterns with its own lark grammar for the subset and lowers them to clingo rules over the record's facts, so the logic core stays the one engine. A chain names a pattern in `relation` or `sibling` as it names a field: the pattern's two ends are the step, and its named inner nodes render as "through". A partial match is no step and luria derives nothing from it. The subset is checked against the schemes at load and is stratified by construction. Rejected: a field list on the scheme, clingo rule bodies as queries, a graph engine, grand-cypher over networkx, Raqlet, GraphGlot as the parser, and built-in open ends. | Proposed |
| [ADR-132](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-132.md) | A named path pattern may render a page of its matches | A pattern with an `output:` (and optional `title:`) renders there as a view luria supplies, `luria:pattern.md.j2`: one row per match, one column per named node. It is a list, never a finding; `report: true` is the separate lint consumer, a pattern may have both, and acknowledged matches stay listed. Every path luria renders is checked against every other at load. Rejected: a renderer of its own, closing the issue as served by views, a `reports:` family, fixed placement, and grouping rows. | Proposed |
| [ADR-133](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-133.md) | A pattern page nests its matches as an outline, and patterns may share one | A pattern page renders as an outline by default: each match is the path of its named nodes, matches merge by shared prefix, and each node is written by the step renderer chain pages use, with `facet_by` as on a chain. `layout: table` keeps [ADR-132](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-132.md)'s flat table. Patterns naming one `output` merge by position into one outline, which draws claim, argument and undercutter at fixed depth with no change to chains. Reverses [ADR-132](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-132.md)'s deferral of grouping. Rejected: grouping by the first column only, `OPTIONAL MATCH`, and a `pages:` family. Unbounded-depth threads stay a chain's. | Proposed |
| [ADR-135](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-135.md) | A pattern node may test its own field for inequality or membership | The path-pattern subset of [ADR-129](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-129.md) gains one comparison per node, written inside the node in Cypher's inline node predicate: `(p:CLAIM WHERE p.status <> 'Active')`, `(o:CLAIM WHERE o.status IN ['Proposed', 'Active'])` and `(n WHERE NOT n.status IN [...])`. The comparison tests the node's own field, so it stays local to the node and readable in the line. It lowers to the `status/2` and `value/4` literals the property map already uses, plus negation over facts, so every program stays stratified. A document without the field matches no comparison, as with Cypher's null. Rejected: a list-valued property map (`{status: ['Proposed', 'Open']}`), a path-level `WHERE` clause with `AND`/`OR`, `=` as a second spelling of the map, nested `WHERE NOT`, and keeping the subset and a script beside it. | Proposed |
| [ADR-136](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-136.md) | luria repair writes what the committed sources imply; link --fix writes what the working tree's change implies | `luria repair` runs in CI on every pull request and on the default branch, and `luria link --fix` runs only where an author runs it, so a write that lives only in the second piles up wherever nobody runs it. Nucleation carried 812 one-sided converse pairs that way. The rule: a write belongs in `repair` when its answer is a function of the committed sources and the configuration alone, so any checkout of a commit computes the same edits, a second run computes none, and the lint can name `repair` as the remedy. It belongs only in `link --fix` when it needs what a checkout does not have, namely the author's uncommitted change against HEAD, which [ADR-084](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-084.md)'s completion reads. A judgement belongs in neither ([ADR-119](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-119.md)). `link --fix` may also run a repair, as it does the linking, but no repair waits on it. Applied here, [ADR-137](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-137.md)'s normalization of a directed pair is a repair. Rejected: everything mechanical into `repair` (it would run [ADR-084](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-084.md)'s HEAD-relative completion in CI, where HEAD is the tree), splitting by how often a write is needed, and a third command. | Proposed |
| [ADR-137](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-137.md) | A directed converse pair stores its primary side; the derived side is computed | Supersedes [ADR-084](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-084.md) for directed pairs. A converse pair marks its derived side with `derived: true` on that side's reference. Only the primary side is stored, and every reader gets the derived side from `relations.edges()`. The derived field may still be written, and `luria repair` moves what is written there. Where the primary side already holds the edge, the derived entry is dropped. Where it does not, the entry becomes the primary entry on the other document. A move that would assert a directed relation both ways, break a document's contract, or name no document is reported and left as filed. With nothing stored twice there is no HEAD baseline to consult for a directed pair, so a deletion is final. Symmetric relations, and pairs that declare no direction, keep [ADR-084](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-084.md)'s rule. The latter are reported as `undirected-relations` rather than refused. `one-sided-relations` now covers only those two kinds, and a hand-filed derived entry is `derived-relations`. Fired on Nucleation: 2,626 derived entries dropped, 62 moved, 1,256 files, the relation graph unchanged at 10,815 edges. Rejected: `primary: true` on the forward side, refusing undirected pairs, completion run in CI, and keeping both sides stored. | Proposed |
| [ADR-138](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-138.md) | luria repair prunes acknowledgements that excuse nothing only when asked, and checks the findings did not move | `luria repair --prune_stale` removes the codes in `inactive-ok`, `unresolved-ok` and `mention-ok` directives that answer for no site, and deletes a directive left naming nothing. Removing them provably changes no finding, and the repair checks it: it re-scans after writing and restores every file if any citation's standing moved. It is opt-in, because [ADR-119](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-119.md)'s line still holds: an uncited directive may mean its citation moved, and whether to move or delete the directive is a judgement. The flag is a person making that judgement for the whole tree. A record can make it once for good with `repair.prune_stale: true` in luria.yaml, as it can every `repair` flag, so CI prunes without the workflow passing it. Rejected: pruning in the default repair, as [#385](https://github.com/dmarx/luria/issues/385) first proposed; a lint check that relation-field citations need no excuse (they are already blanked, so such a directive is already reported); and leaving it to hand-written scripts, which on Nucleation misread the report and had to be run twice. | Proposed |
| [ADR-139](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-139.md) | The record description is rendered from a template luria ships, with its prose in the template and its facts from the config | `docs/record.md` was built from Python strings: a header constant, eight section introductions in a tuple, and a markdown table assembled in each section function. It is now `luria:record.md.j2`, rendered in the sandbox [ADR-130](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-130.md)'s views use. `record_doc.context` gives the template facts read from the loaded config and no prose. The template holds every heading, introduction, table and empty-state line, so the page's text is edited in one place, and a section with nothing to show is left out by the template, heading and all. The output was byte-identical on luria's record, nucleation's, a fresh init, and three fixtures covering every empty and partial case. Rejected: registering the page as a view luria supplies, which would link it and so send the luria decisions its prose cites to the project's own; letting a project override the template, deferred until one asks; and keeping the strings. | Proposed |
